Updated assessment using the Beige Book: While the statement emphasizes “strong fundamentals,” the intermeeting 50 bp cut and expanded liquidity operations point to a clear risk‑management posture. Beige Book reports around this time cited the coronavirus as a growing risk already depressing travel and tourism, pressuring some prices, and disrupting manufacturing supply chains and transportation. Conditions varied across districts, with areas of growth in nonfinancial services but weakness in natural resource extraction and softer loan growth. Layered onto SLOOS indications of tighter credit standards and weaker loan demand, these Beige Book signals amplify downside risks to activity and funding beyond money market pressures. Overall tone: defensive and precautionary despite still‑solid starting conditions.
